content: Select a checksummed Linux AMD64 release archive and a normalized release ID from the exact protected source head.
Verify the archive digest and members, create a root-owned immutable versioned release, and reject traversal or conflicting bytes.
Create or verify the dedicated non-login service identity, private environment boundary, hardened systemd unit, and loopback service profile.
Verify the service process UID, effective hardening properties, active release pointer, and unauthenticated HTTP 401 boundary.
Create one synthetic governed default and one synthetic operator token whose raw value remains outside logs and evidence.
Use the synthetic token to prove the running service reads the governed default through the restricted PostgreSQL role.
Install a second checksummed release, move the former current target to previous, restart, and verify the new release is healthy.
Activate a checksummed synthetic failing release and require the installer to restore and verify the prior healthy release before returning failure.
Explicitly roll back to the first release, verify health, then roll forward to the second release through the same reversible pointer contract.
Create a private PostgreSQL custom-format backup through a libpq service name with no owner or ACL replay and publish checksum plus normalized metadata.
Reject a digest mismatch and reject restoration over a target that already contains Vermory authority tables.
Restore the verified dump into an empty target, replay migrations, grant an existing restricted runtime role, and rebuild disposable projections.
Change only the private runtime database configuration, restart the same installed service, and keep the admin identity outside the process.
Prove the restored token digest authenticates and the restored governed default is visible after the service restart.
Retain normalized hashes, statuses, hardening properties, backup metadata, failure evidence, and explicit non-claims without credentials or raw tokens.
